claims.text: Conventionally processed eutectic high-entropy alloys have dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
The conventionally processed lamellar-colony baseline exhibits brittle room-temperature tensile behavior and low tensile ductility.
Post-solution-treatment aging at approximately 450–500 °C for 4–8 hours will induce nanoscale precipitation.
The induced nanoscale precipitates will be distributed uniformly along lamellar interfaces or colony boundaries.
Boundary precipitates will improve load transfer between the constituent phases.
Boundary precipitates will blunt or suppress microcrack initiation.
Boundary precipitates will blunt or suppress microcrack propagation.
The nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates will increase strength.
Reinforcement of the interlamellar regions will toughen critical boundaries and increase tensile ductility.
The aging treatment will increase ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated lamellar-colony baseline.
The aging treatment will increase room-temperature elongation to failure relative to the untreated lamellar-colony baseline.
The simultaneous strength and ductility benefit requires the precipitates to remain nanoscale and uniformly distributed.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or overaging may degrade ductility.
The intervention is expected to be effective primarily in eutectic alloys with similar dual-phase lamellar morphologies.
